references.text: Jesus had already earlier set his course toward Jerusalem ([ref:Luk 9:51-53|Luke 9:51-53]). Here the journey through Samaria is also mentioned, which forms the background for the meeting with Samaritans along the way.

Jesus' journey toward Jerusalem is a recurring theme in the Gospel of Luke. In [ref:Luk 13:22|Luke 13:22] it is described that he traveled through cities and villages, teaching as he made his way to Jerusalem.

The journey toward Jerusalem reaches its climax in [ref:Luk 18:31|Luke 18:31], where Jesus tells the disciples that they are now going up to Jerusalem, where everything written by the prophets about the Son of Man will be fulfilled.
In [ref:Luk 9:56|Luke 9:56] Jesus and his disciples continued on to another village after being rejected in Samaria, showing the same travel route through the border area between Samaria and Galilee.
In [ref:Joh 4:4|John 4:4] Jesus had to travel through Samaria, which shows that the natural route between Galilee and Jerusalem went through Samaritan territory.

The connection with Samaria in this verse prepares for the story of the ten lepers, where it turns out that the one who was grateful was a Samaritan ([ref:Luk 17:16|Luke 17:16]). The fact that Jesus traveled through the border area between Samaria and Galilee explains why lepers from both groups were together.
[ref:Luk 19:11|Luke 19:11] marks that Jesus is approaching Jerusalem, showing the gradual advance toward the goal that begins already in Luke 17:11.
Also in [ref:Mark 10:32|Mark 10:32] it is described that Jesus was on his way up to Jerusalem, and the disciples followed him with fear and awe. This shows the same travel motif toward Jerusalem.
